MOCK_CAVA.service_note: Bone dry, high acid. The opener for anyone who says "nothing too sweet".

MOCK_PETNAT.service_note: Cloudy on purpose — say so before you pour. Low ABV, slight funk, crowd-splitter.

MOCK_CHAMP.service_note: Grower Champagne, not a big house. Worth the upsell from the cava — say "same family farms it".

MOCK_MOVIA.service_note: Disgorged at the table, upside down, in a bucket. Twenty minutes of theatre — only offer it if you have time.

MOCK_ALBA.service_note: Saline and briny. Sell it with anything from the sea.

MOCK_RIES.service_note: Off-dry but reads dry. Best thing on the list for anything spicy.

MOCK_MASSICAN.service_note: Napa making Italian whites. The answer for a table that cannot agree.

MOCK_SANC.service_note: Benchmark Sancerre, biodynamic. Vintage rolled in June — confirm before you quote it.

MOCK_CHARD.service_note: No new oak. Lead with "not a buttery Chardonnay" — it heads off the objection.

MOCK_SKIN.service_note: Orange wine — tannic for a white. Always offer a taste first. It splits the room.

MOCK_ROSE.service_note: Pale, bone dry, high-altitude fruit. The default pour on a warm afternoon.

MOCK_LIEUDIT.service_note: Herbal, a little savoury. For someone who thinks they dislike rosé.

MOCK_BANDOL.service_note: The serious one. Structured enough for the chicken. Worth the price, and say why.

MOCK_GAMAY.service_note: Cru Beaujolais, served with a chill. The gateway red — it converts white drinkers.

MOCK_STOUMEN.service_note: Juicy, low tannin, drinks like a grown-up soda. Best value red on the list.

MOCK_BOWARROW.service_note: Loire methods in Oregon. Serve it properly cold, not cellar temp.

MOCK_MENCIA.service_note: Volcanic, high acid, almost no oak. Serve with a slight chill.

MOCK_NEBB.service_note: Rose petal and tar, grippy. For the Pinot drinker who wants more.

MOCK_PINOT.service_note: Highest-margin pour on the list. Vintage rolled — confirm before quoting.

MOCK_CAB.service_note: Needs air. Decant it if the table is staying for dinner.

MOCK_MONTE.service_note: Two left. Manager approval before opening. Decant a full hour.

MOCK_SPRITZ.service_note: Build in the glass, no shake. House aperitif — offer it first.

MOCK_PALOMA.service_note: Fresh grapefruit, not soda. Salt the rim unless they say no.

MOCK_GARDEN.service_note: Low ABV, very drinkable at brunch. Dill is fresh, not syrup.

MOCK_FIZZ.service_note: Named for the room. Strawberry is macerated in-house, changes with the season.

MOCK_SOUR.service_note: Contains raw egg white — flag it. Can be made without, ask for a "dry sour".

MOCK_ESPMART.service_note: Caffeine — do not sell it to a 9pm table without saying so.

MOCK_BLOODY.service_note: House mix has Worcestershire — contains anchovy. Not vegetarian.

MOCK_MIMOSA.service_note: Juice rotates. Ask the bar what is on before you promise anything.

MOCK_GARDEN0.service_note: The best N/A option. Serve it in the same glass as the real spritz — it matters.

MOCK_GHIA.service_note: Properly bitter. For someone who misses an aperitivo.

MOCK_SHRUB.service_note: Shrub is made weekly. Sweet-tart, the one kids order.

MOCK_KSA.service_note: The house beer. Light, safe, always moving.

MOCK_PILS.service_note: Brewed in Berkeley to an Austrian recipe. Very dry.

MOCK_IPA.service_note: 8% — mention it. Allocation is limited, check before promising a second.

MOCK_CIDER.service_note: Naturally gluten-free — the answer for a coeliac table.

MOCK_NONINO.service_note: Gentle, orange-peel sweet. The one to start someone on.

MOCK_FERNET.service_note: This is San Francisco. Serve it cold, no ceremony.

MOCK_CARDA.service_note: Wine-based, low ABV, cardoon and thistle. Good before dinner, not only after.

MOCK_BRAULIO.service_note: Alpine, minty, almost medicinal. Sell it after something rich.
